# Synthetic video fixtures

The video fixtures contain FFmpeg's generated `testsrc2` pattern (160x90,
15 fps), not recorder footage. Each access unit includes an AUD.

`ip.h264`: libx264 ultrafast, 30 frames, keyint/min-keyint 15, scenecut 0,
bframes 0, aud 1.

`ip.h265`: libx265 ultrafast, 30 frames, keyint/min-keyint 15, scenecut 0,
bframes 0, repeat-headers 1, aud 1, pools 1, frame-threads 1.

`b.h265`: the same HEVC generator with 24 frames, keyint/min-keyint 12,
bframes 3. This verifies default-mode rejection of B-frame timing; support
requires the separate, validated fixed-GOP opt-in.

`b.h264`: libx264 veryfast, 45 frames, keyint/min-keyint 15, scenecut 0,
bframes 2, b-adapt 0, b-pyramid none, aud 1.

`b-closed.h265`: libx265 ultrafast, 45 frames, keyint/min-keyint 15,
scenecut 0, bframes 3, b-adapt 0, open-gop 0, repeat-headers 1, aud 1,
pools 1, frame-threads 1. Both 45-frame fixtures have three closed GOPs.
`picture_test.go` checks their POC and slice type against independent FFmpeg
decoded-frame `pkt_pos` ordering. These are codec tests, not evidence of Exacq
wire timestamp semantics. The separate recorder and actual-SDK correlation,
fixed-count timing fixtures and supported opt-in are documented in
[B-picture research](../../../docs/exacq/b-pictures.md).

`config.xml` is a hand-sanitized configuration fixture owned by the inventory
tests; it contains no recorder or camera credentials.

`spakeplus.json` contains synthetic authentication vectors generated by the
pinned SDK in an isolated process. Every username, password, salt, scalar and
recorder identity is invented for testing. No recorder session or account was
used. Reproduction and evidence are in `docs/exacq/spakeplus.md`.

`health-partial-status.json` contains sanitized transport metadata from an
observed retained-session health failure. It records only packet type/subtype,
status, byte counts, known XML field names and section presence. It contains no
wire payloads, recorder identities, device settings, MACs, passwords or keys.
